    61→
    62→**When generating new code, match the style, naming, and patterns from these examples exactly.**
    63→
    64→---
    65→
    66→## Architecture Principles
    67→
    68→### Gradle Multimodule Structure
    69→
    70→Always organize projects with clear module boundaries:
    71→
    72→```
    73→app/                    # Platform entry points (thin shells)
    74→  androidApp/           # Android app module (Activity + KoinApp)
    75→  desktopApp/           # Desktop app module (Window + KoinApp)
    76→  webApp/               # Web app module (ComposeViewport + KoinApp)
    77→composeApp/             # Shared Compose application (main app composable)
    78→core/                   # Core business logic
    79→  coreCommon/           # Platform services, dispatchers, utilities
    80→  corePref/             # Preferences/DataStore management
    81→navigation/             # Navigation setup (Jetpack Navigation3)
    82→ui/                     # UI feature modules
    83→  uiCommon/             # Shared theme, resources, common components
    84→  uiMain/               # Feature: main screen
    85→  uiSplash/             # Feature: splash screen
    86→convention-plugin-multiplatform/  # Custom Gradle convention plugins
    87→```
    88→
    89→**Key rules:**
    90→- Platform app modules are thin shells — they only call `KoinApp()` composable
    91→- Each feature gets its own `ui/ui*` module
    92→- Core logic lives in `core/` modules, independent of UI
    93→- Navigation is a standalone module implementing all navigation callbacks
    94→- Convention plugins centralize all KMP build configuration
    95→
    96→### Convention Plugin Pattern
    97→
    98→Use precompiled script plugins in `convention-plugin-multiplatform/` to avoid repeating KMP configuration:
    99→
   100→```kotlin
   101→// convention-plugin-multiplatform/src/main/kotlin/composeMultiplatformConvention.gradle.kts
   102→plugins {
   103→    id("org.jetbrains.kotlin.multiplatform")
   104→    id("org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose")
   105→    id("org.jetbrains.compose")
   106→    id("com.android.library")
   107→}
   108→
   109→kotlin {
   110→    androidTarget()
   111→    jvm()
   112→    js(IR) { browser() }
   113→    wasmJs { browser() }
   114→    listOf(iosArm64(), iosSimulatorArm64()).forEach {
   115→        it.binaries.framework { baseName = project.name; isStatic = true }
   116→    }
   117→
   118→    sourceSets {
   119→        commonMain.dependencies {
   120→            // shared dependencies
   121→        }
   122→    }
   123→}
   124→```
   125→
   126→Then every module simply applies:
   127→```kotlin
   128→plugins {
   129→    id("composeMultiplatformConvention")
   130→}
   131→```
   132→
   133→**Version catalog access in convention plugins** — use this pattern:
   134→```kotlin
   135→// convention-plugin-multiplatform/build.gradle.kts
   136→dependencies {
   137→    implementation(files(libs.javaClass.superclass.protectionDomain.codeSource.location))
   138→}
   139→```
   140→
   141→### Dependency Management
   142→
   143→- Use **Gradle Version Catalog** (`gradle/libs.versions.toml`) for all dependency versions
   144→- Use **type-safe project accessors** (`TYPESAFE_PROJECT_ACCESSORS` in settings):
   145→  ```kotlin
   146→  implementation(projects.core.coreCommon)
   147→  implementation(projects.ui.uiCommon)
   148→  ```
   149→- Use **Koin BOM** for consistent DI versions:
   150→  ```kotlin
   151→  implementation(project.dependencies.platform(libs.koin.bom))
   152→  ```
   153→
   154→### Source Set Structure
   155→
   156→Every KMP module follows this consistent layout:
   157→```
   158→src/
   159→  commonMain/kotlin/       # Shared code (majority of code lives here)
   160→  commonTest/kotlin/       # Shared tests
   161→  androidMain/kotlin/      # Android-specific (expect/actual implementations)
   162→  androidHostTest/kotlin/  # Android Robolectric/screenshot tests
   163→  jvmMain/kotlin/          # Desktop-specific
   164→  jvmTest/kotlin/          # Desktop tests
   165→  iosMain/kotlin/          # iOS-specific
   166→  iosTest/kotlin/          # iOS tests
   167→  webMain/kotlin/          # Web-specific (JS + Wasm shared)
   168→```
   169→
   170→---
   171→
   172→## Core Patterns
   173→
   174→### Expect/Actual
   175→
   176→Use expect/actual for platform-specific implementations:
   177→
   178→**Pattern 1 — Koin DI Modules:**
   179→```kotlin
   180→// commonMain
   181→expect val corePrefModule: Module
   182→
   183→// androidMain
   184→actual val corePrefModule = module {
   185→    single { createDataStore(get<Context>()) }
   186→}
   187→
   188→// jvmMain
   189→actual val corePrefModule = module {
   190→    single { createDataStore() }
   191→}
   192→```
   193→
   194→**Pattern 2 — Platform Services:**
   195→```kotlin
   196→// commonMain - define interface
   197→interface PlatformService { ... }
   198→
   199→// Platform-specific implementations in androidMain, jvmMain, iosMain, webMain
   200→```
   201→
   202→**Pattern 3 — Coroutine Dispatchers:**
   203→```kotlin
   204→// commonMain
   205→interface DispatcherSet {
   206→    val default: CoroutineDispatcher
   207→    val io: CoroutineDispatcher
   208→    val main: CoroutineDispatcher
   209→}
   210→// Each platform provides actual dispatcher implementations
   211→```
   212→
   213→### MVVM Architecture per Feature
   214→
   215→Every UI feature module follows this structure:
   216→```
   217→ui/uiFeature/
   218→  src/commonMain/kotlin/
   219→    FeatureScreen.kt           # Composable UI (stateful + stateless)
   220→    FeatureViewModel.kt        # State management + business logic
   221→    FeatureViewState.kt        # Sealed class: Loading / Success / Error
   222→    FeatureViewEvent.kt        # User interaction events
   223→    FeatureNavigationCallback.kt  # Navigation actions interface
   224→    FeaturePreviewData.kt      # Preview composables for testing
   225→```
   226→
   227→**ViewModel pattern:**
   228→```kotlin
   229→class FeatureViewModel(
   230→    private val navigationCallback: FeatureNavigationCallback,
   231→) : ViewModel() {
   232→    val viewState: StateFlow<FeatureViewState>
   233→        field = MutableStateFlow<FeatureViewState>(FeatureViewState.Loading)
   234→
   235→    fun onEvent(event: FeatureViewEvent) { ... }
   236→}
   237→```
   238→
   239→**Screen pattern — separate stateful and stateless:**
   240→```kotlin
   241→@Composable
   242→fun FeatureScreen(viewModel: FeatureViewModel) {
   243→    val viewState by viewModel.viewState.collectAsState()
   244→    FeatureScreenContent(viewState = viewState, onEvent = viewModel::onEvent)
   245→}
   246→
   247→@Composable
   248→fun FeatureScreenContent(viewState: FeatureViewState, onEvent: (FeatureViewEvent) -> Unit) {
   249→    // Pure UI, no side effects — easy to preview and test
   250→}
   251→```
   252→
   253→### Dependency Injection with Koin
   254→
   255→- Each module defines its own Koin module
   256→- Platform-specific modules provide platform dependencies
   257→- ViewModels created via factory with parameters:
   258→  ```kotlin
   259→  factory { params -> FeatureViewModel(navigationCallback = params[0]) }
   260→  ```
   261→
   262→### Navigation with Jetpack Navigation3
   263→
   264→- Type-safe routes using `@Serializable` data objects/classes
   265→- Backstack managed with `mutableStateListOf<NavKey>`
   266→- Central `AppNavigation` class implements all feature navigation callbacks
   267→- Navigation module depends on all feature modules
   268→
   269→---
   270→
   271→## Testing Strategy
   272→
   273→### Screenshot Testing with Roborazzi
   274→
   275→- Integrated across modules for visual regression testing
   276→- Platform-specific screenshot tests: Android (Robolectric), Desktop, iOS
   277→- Screenshots stored in `src/screenshots/` per module
   278→- Run with `-DIS_DATA_STUB_ENABLED=true` for deterministic output
   279→- Record: `./gradlew recordRoborazzi`
   280→- Verify: `./gradlew verifyRoborazzi`
   281→
   282→### Test Configuration
   283→
   284→- **Android**: Managed virtual devices (Pixel 2, API 35), animations disabled
   285→- **Desktop**: JVM tests with Compose UI test framework
   286→- **iOS**: Simulator tests on arm64
   287→- **Web**: `wasmJsBrowserTest`
   288→- Use `@OptIn(ExperimentalTestApi::class)` for Compose UI testing
   289→
   290→---
   291→
   292→## CI/CD Best Practices
   293→
   294→### GitHub Actions Structure
   295→
   296→1. **Lint job**: ktlintFormat (auto-commit) -> ktlintCheck, detekt, lint
   297→2. **Test matrix**: jvmTest, wasmJsBrowserTest, Android instrumented, iOS simulator
   298→3. **Screenshot verification**: Dynamic matrix generation scanning for Roborazzi plugin
   299→4. **Platform builds**: Separate jobs for Android, Desktop, Web, iOS
   300→
   301→### Dynamic Screenshot Matrix
   302→
   303→Use custom build logic to scan subprojects for Roborazzi plugin and generate a CI matrix:
   304→```kotlin
   305→// buildSrc - ScreenshotJobsMatrix.kt
   306→// Scans all subprojects, finds those with Roborazzi, generates JSON matrix
   307→```
   308→
   309→---
   310→
   311→## Gradle Performance
   312→
   313→```properties
   314→# gradle.properties
   315→org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx6G
   316→org.gradle.caching=true
   317→org.gradle.configuration-cache=true
   318→org.gradle.parallel=true
   319→kotlin.daemon.jvmargs=-Xmx6G
   320→```
   321→
   322→---
   323→
   324→## Common Commands
   325→
   326→| Task | Command |
   327→|------|---------|
   328→| Android build | `./gradlew app:androidApp:assembleDebug` |
   329→| Desktop run | `./gradlew :app:desktopApp:run` |
   330→| Desktop hot reload | `./gradlew :app:desktopApp:hotRun --auto` |
   331→| Web (Wasm) run | `./gradlew :app:webApp:wasmJsBrowserDevelopmentRun` |
   332→| Web (JS) run | `./gradlew :app:webApp:jsBrowserDevelopmentRun` |
   333→| All JVM tests | `./gradlew jvmTest` |
   334→| iOS tests | `./gradlew iosSimulatorArm64Test` |
   335→| Web tests | `./gradlew :app:webApp:wasmJsBrowserTest` |
   336→| Android tests | `./gradlew managedVirtualDeviceDebugAndroidTest` |
   337→| Format code | `./gradlew ktlintFormat` |
   338→| Lint checks | `./gradlew ktlintCheck detekt lint` |
   339→| Record screenshots | `./gradlew recordRoborazzi` |
   340→| Verify screenshots | `./gradlew verifyRoborazzi` |
   341→
   342→---
   343→
   344→## When Advising on KMP Projects
   345→
   346→1. **Always maximize shared code in `commonMain`** — platform-specific code should be minimal
   347→2. **Use convention plugins** — never duplicate build configuration across modules
   348→3. **One feature = one module** — keeps build times low and separation clean
   349→4. **App modules are thin shells** — all logic lives in shared modules
   350→5. **Prefer interfaces in commonMain** with platform implementations via expect/actual or DI
   351→6. **Version catalog for everything** — no hardcoded versions in build files
   352→7. **Screenshot tests for every screen** — catch visual regressions automatically
   353→8. **Type-safe navigation** — use serializable routes, not string-based navigation
   354→9. **Stateless composables** — separate state management from UI rendering for testability
   355→10. **DataStore over SharedPreferences** — multiplatform-compatible preferences
   356→

## Ktor Latest Stable Version for KMP (as of February 2026)

### Latest Stable Version: 3.4.0

Released January 23, 2026. Ktor 3.4.0 is built with **Kotlin 2.3.0**, confirmed from its `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. This means it is fully compatible with Kotlin 2.3.x (including 2.3.10 once released, as patch versions are backwards-compatible within the same minor).

> Note: Ktor 3.4.0 has one caveat — its experimental **OpenAPI generation** feature has a known issue with Kotlin 2.3.0-RC due to a compiler plugin binary compatibility issue. This does not affect standard client/server usage or KMP networking.

---

### Group ID

All Ktor artifacts share the same group:

```
io.ktor
```

---

### Complete Maven Coordinates (version: 3.4.0)

| Purpose | Maven Coordinate |
|---|---|
| Core (commonMain) | `io.ktor:ktor-client-core:3.4.0` |
| Android engine (OkHttp) | `io.ktor:ktor-client-okhttp:3.4.0` |
| JVM Desktop engine (CIO) | `io.ktor:ktor-client-cio:3.4.0` |
| JVM Desktop engine (OkHttp alt) | `io.ktor:ktor-client-okhttp:3.4.0` |
| iOS engine (Darwin/NSURLSession) | `io.ktor:ktor-client-darwin:3.4.0` |
| JS/WasmJS engine | `io.ktor:ktor-client-js:3.4.0` |
| Content negotiation plugin | `io.ktor:ktor-client-content-negotiation:3.4.0` |
| kotlinx.serialization JSON adapter | `io.ktor:ktor-serialization-kotlinx-json:3.4.0` |
| BOM (optional, for version management) | `io.ktor:ktor-bom:3.4.0` |
| Version catalog (optional) | `io.ktor:ktor-version-catalog:3.4.0` |

**Engine platform support notes:**
- `ktor-client-okhttp` — JVM + Android (requires OkHttp 4.x)
- `ktor-client-cio` — JVM, Android, Native, JS, WasmJS (pure Kotlin, no native deps)
- `ktor-client-android` — Android-only legacy engine (prefer `ktor-client-okhttp` for Android)
- `ktor-client-darwin` — iOS, macOS, tvOS, watchOS (uses NSURLSession)
- `ktor-client-js` — Kotlin/JS and WasmJS targets

---

### Gradle Plugin

Ktor does **not** have its own Gradle plugin for the client library itself. Dependencies are added directly. There is a **Ktor project generator plugin** (`io.ktor.plugin`) used for server-side fat JAR generation, but it is not needed for KMP client projects.

---

### Recommended `libs.versions.toml` (Version Catalog)

```toml
[versions]
ktor = "3.4.0"

[libraries]
ktor-client-core                  = { module = "io.ktor:ktor-client-core",                  version.ref = "ktor" }
ktor-client-okhttp                = { module = "io.ktor:ktor-client-okhttp",                version.ref = "ktor" }
ktor-client-cio                   = { module = "io.ktor:ktor-client-cio",                   version.ref = "ktor" }
ktor-client-darwin                = { module = "io.ktor:ktor-client-darwin",                version.ref = "ktor" }
ktor-client-js                    = { module = "io.ktor:ktor-client-js",                    version.ref = "ktor" }
ktor-client-content-negotiation   = { module = "io.ktor:ktor-client-content-negotiation",   version.ref = "ktor" }
ktor-serialization-kotlinx-json   = { module = "io.ktor:ktor-serialization-kotlinx-json",   version.ref = "ktor" }
```

---

### Recommended `build.gradle.kts` (KMP sourceSet wiring)

```kotlin
kotlin {
    sourceSets {
        commonMain.dependencies {
            implementation(libs.ktor.client.core)
            implementation(libs.ktor.client.content.negotiation)
            implementation(libs.ktor.serialization.kotlinx.json)
        }
        androidMain.dependencies {
            implementation(libs.ktor.client.okhttp)
        }
        desktopMain.dependencies {
            implementation(libs.ktor.client.cio)  // or ktor.client.okhttp
        }
        iosMain.dependencies {
            implementation(libs.ktor.client.darwin)
        }
        jsMain.dependencies {
            implementation(libs.ktor.client.js)
        }
        wasmJsMain.dependencies {
            implementation(libs.ktor.client.js)
        }
    }
}
```

---

### Android vs JVM Desktop Engine Choice

| Scenario | Recommended Engine | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Android | `ktor-client-okhttp` | Best performance, battle-tested, supports duplex streaming (new in 3.4.0) |
| JVM Desktop | `ktor-client-cio` | Pure Kotlin, no extra deps, supports coroutines natively |
| JVM Desktop (alt) | `ktor-client-okhttp` | If you prefer OkHttp's ecosystem on desktop too |

Write all `commonMain` Kotlin source files for the `client` KMP module of a book reading leaderboard app.

## Project root: `/Users/se/git/cc-experiments`
## Package root: `com.bookreads`
## Source root: `client/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/bookreads/`

## DTOs from `shared-dto` (import `com.bookreads.dto.*`):
```kotlin
data class UserDto(val id: Long, val username: String, val createdAt: String)
data class SessionSyncRequest(val clientId: String, val username: String, val bookTitle: String, val startedAt: String, val endedAt: String?, val durationSec: Long)
data class SessionDto(val clientId: String, val username: String, val bookTitle: String, val startedAt: String, val endedAt: String?, val durationSec: Long)
data class LeaderboardEntryDto(val rank: Int, val username: String, val totalSec: Long, val sessionCount: Int)
```

## REST API (base path `/api/v1`):
- `POST /users` body `{username}` → `UserDto`
- `GET /users/{username}` → `UserDto`
- `POST /sessions/sync` body `SessionSyncRequest` → `SessionDto`
- `GET /sessions/{clientId}` → `SessionDto?`
- `GET /leaderboard?window=daily|weekly|monthly|alltime` → `List<LeaderboardEntryDto>`

---

## Files to create

### 1. `api/BookApi.kt`
Ktor `HttpClient`-based implementation. Use `ContentNegotiation` + `kotlinx.serialization` plugin (configured via Koin injection of `HttpClient`).

Define interface + Ktor implementation:
```kotlin
interface BookApi {
    suspend fun registerUser(username: String): UserDto
    suspend fun getUser(username: String): UserDto?
    suspend fun syncSession(request: SessionSyncRequest): SessionDto
    suspend fun getSession(clientId: String): SessionDto?
    suspend fun getLeaderboard(window: String): List<LeaderboardEntryDto>
}
```

`KtorBookApi` takes `(httpClient: HttpClient, baseUrl: String)`. For `getUser` and `getSession`, return `null` on 404. For all others, throw on error. Use `io.ktor.client.call.body()`.

### 2. `storage/AppPreferences.kt`
```kotlin
package com.bookreads.storage

import kotlinx.serialization.Serializable

@Serializable
data class AppPreferences(
    val username: String? = null,
    val activeSession: ActiveSession? = null,
)

@Serializable
data class ActiveSession(
    val clientId: String,
    val bookTitle: String,
    val startedAt: String,
    val elapsedSec: Long,
)
```

### 3. `storage/LocalStorageService.kt`
```kotlin
package com.bookreads.storage

import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.Flow

interface LocalStorageService {
    fun getUsername(): Flow<String?>
    suspend fun setUsername(username: String?)
    fun getActiveSession(): Flow<ActiveSession?>
    suspend fun saveActiveSession(session: ActiveSession)
    suspend fun clearActiveSession()
}
```

### 4. `session/LocalSessionStore.kt`
Wraps `LocalStorageService`. Delegates all calls to the service. No extra logic:
```kotlin
class LocalSessionStore(private val storage: LocalStorageService) {
    fun getActiveSession(): Flow<ActiveSession?> = storage.getActiveSession()
    suspend fun saveActiveSession(session: ActiveSession) = storage.saveActiveSession(session)
    suspend fun clearActiveSession() = storage.clearActiveSession()
}
```

### 5. `sync/SessionSyncService.kt`

content.thinking:
Good progress - the build configuration errors are fixed. Now there's a dependency resolution error:

```
Could not find androidx.datastore:datastore-core-okio:1.2.0.
Required by: project ':client'

The project declares repositories, effectively ignoring the repositories you have declared in the settings.
```

The error says "The project declares repositories, effectively ignoring the repositories you have declared in the settings." This means the `client` module (or the `android-library` plugin) is declaring project-level repositories, which overrides the central `dependencyResolutionManagement` in `settings.gradle.kts`. 

The `google()` maven repository is needed for `androidx.datastore`. Currently, the `settings.gradle.kts` has `google()` in `dependencyResolutionManagement`, but the Google repository is filtered with `includeGroupByRegex` to only include `com.android.*`, `com.google.*`, `androidx.*`, `android.*` groups. This should include `androidx.datastore`.
 
The issue is that a plugin like AGP is adding repositories at the project level, which takes precedence over the settings-level configuration. I need to either adjust the `repositoriesMode` setting to `PREFER_SETTINGS` or add `google()` directly to the client module's build file. The issue is that `repositoriesMode` determines whether settings or project-level repositories take precedence, and the AGP plugin declares repositories at the project level. Good progress! The repository issue is fixed (only a warning about ktlint.gradle using MavenRepo). Now there's a new error:

```
The Compose Compiler requires the Compose Runtime to be on the class path, but none could be found.
```

This means the `compose.compiler` plugin is applied to the `client` module, but the Compose runtime is not on the classpath for the JVM compilation. The Compose compiler plugin was included in `client/build.gradle.kts` for future Phase 3, but since the Compose runtime libraries aren't added to `commonMain.dependencies`, the compiler plugin fails.

The fix: Either:


1. Add Compose runtime to the classpath (add `implementation(compose.runtime)` to `commonMain.dependencies`)

# Book Reading Leaderboard — Project Plan

## Overview

A real-time leaderboard application that tracks how much time users spend reading. Users pick a display name, start/stop a single reading session at a time (tagged with a book title), and compete on a shared global leaderboard across daily, weekly, monthly, and all-time windows.

---

## Requirements Summary

| Dimension | Decision                                 |
|---|------------------------------------------|
| Leaderboard metric | Total cumulative reading time            |
| Identity | Username only — no auth, no passwords    |
| Book entry | Free-text title (session label)          |
| Concurrent sessions | One active session per user at a time    |
| Session tracking | Client-side (device clock + local state) |
| Backend role | Sync & leaderboard storage only          |
| Leaderboard scope | Global                                   |
| Leaderboard windows | Daily / Weekly / Monthly / All-time      |
| Leaderboard refresh | REST polling (on tab focus + periodic)   |
| Backend framework | Spring Boot (Kotlin)                     |
| Database | PostgreSQL                               |
| Deployment | Docker Compose (local / self-hosted)     |
| Client UI | Compose Multiplatform (shared UI)        |
| Client targets | Android, iOS, JVM Desktop, Web           |

---

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  KMP Client (CMP UI)                 │
│  Android │ iOS │ JVM Desktop │ Web (browser)     │
│                                                      │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│  │           commonMain (shared)                  │  │
│  │  Compose UI · ViewModels · Domain · Ktor HTTP  │  │
│  │  Serialization                                 │  │
│  │                                                │  │
│  │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐  │  │
│  │  │         Session Engine (client-owned)    │  │  │
│  │  │  Local timer · Start/stop control        │  │  │
│  │  │  Persist state · Periodic sync           │  │  │
│  │  └──────────────────────────────────────────┘  │  │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                       │ HTTP REST
┌──────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────┐
│           Spring Boot Backend (Kotlin)               │
│                                                      │
│  Session sync (upsert) · Leaderboard queries         │
│  No session lifecycle logic                          │
│                                                      │
└──────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                       │ JDBC
┌──────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────┐
│                   PostgreSQL                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Repository Structure (Monorepo)

```

├── backend/                          # Spring Boot Gradle module
│   ├── build.gradle.kts
│   └── src/

│           ├── leaderboard/

│           │   └── LeaderboardService.kt

├── client/                           # KMP Gradle module
│   ├── build.gradle.kts
│   └── src/

│       │   ├── model/

---

## Tech Stack

### Backend
| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Language | Kotlin 2.x |
| Framework | Spring Boot 3.x |
| DB access | Spring Data JPA + Hibernate |
| Build | Gradle (Kotlin DSL) |
| Runtime | JVM 21 (virtual threads) |

### Client (KMP)
| Layer | Technology                                                                         |
|---|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Language | Kotlin 2.x Multiplatform                                                           |
| UI | Compose Multiplatform                                                              |
| HTTP | Ktor Client (CIO engine on JVM/Web, Darwin on iOS)                                 |
| Serialization | kotlinx.serialization                                                              |
| Async | Kotlin Coroutines + Flow                                                           |
| DI | Koin Multiplatform                                                                 |
| Navigation | Compose Navigation (multiplatform)                                                 |
| Local storage | `androidx.datastore.core.okio` (Android / iOS / JVM) · `window.localStorage` (Web) |

### Infrastructure
| Component | Technology |
|---|---|
| Database | PostgreSQL 16 |
| Containerization | Docker + Docker Compose |
| Backend container | Eclipse Temurin 21 slim |

---

## Database Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE users (
    id         BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    username   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE reading_sessions (
    id           BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    client_id    TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- client-generated UUID, used for upsert
    user_id      BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
    book_title   TEXT NOT NULL,
    started_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,   -- client-provided timestamp
    ended_at     TIMESTAMPTZ,            -- client-provided; NULL = session still active
    duration_sec BIGINT NOT NULL         -- client-computed and sent on every sync
);

CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_user    ON reading_sessions(user_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_started ON reading_sessions(started_at);
CREATE INDEX idx_sessions_client  ON reading_sessions(client_id);
```

`client_id` is a UUID generated by the client when the session starts. The backend upserts on `client_id`, so repeated syncs (progress updates) update the same row. `duration_sec` is always client-computed — the server never derives it. Leaderboard queries use `WHERE started_at >= :windowStart` on the stored values.

---

## REST API

Base path: `/api/v1`

### Users

| Method | Path | Body | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/users` | `{ "username": "alice" }` | `UserDto` | Register or fetch existing user |
| `GET` | `/users/{username}` | — | `UserDto` | Lookup user |

### Sessions

| Method | Path | Body | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST` | `/sessions/sync` | `SessionSyncRequest` | `SessionDto` | Upsert a session by `clientId`; called on start, periodically while active, and on end |
| `GET` | `/sessions/{clientId}` | — | `SessionDto?` | Fetch last-synced state for a session (used on app restore) |

### Leaderboard

| Method | Path | Params | Response | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/leaderboard` | `window=daily\|weekly\|monthly\|alltime` | `List<LeaderboardEntryDto>` | Ranked list of users by total reading seconds |

---

## DTO Definitions (`shared-dto`)

```kotlin
@Serializable
data class UserDto(val id: Long, val username: String, val createdAt: String)

// Sent by the client on every sync (start, periodic progress, end)
@Serializable
data class SessionSyncRequest(
    val clientId: String,        // client-generated UUID, stable for the session's lifetime
    val username: String,
    val bookTitle: String,
    val startedAt: String,       // ISO-8601, client clock
    val endedAt: String?,        // null while active
    val durationSec: Long        // client-computed elapsed seconds
)

@Serializable
data class SessionDto(
    val clientId: String,
    val username: String,
    val bookTitle: String,
    val startedAt: String,
    val endedAt: String?,
    val durationSec: Long
)

@Serializable
data class LeaderboardEntryDto(
    val rank: Int,
    val username: String,
    val totalSec: Long,
    val sessionCount: Int
)

```

---

## Client Screens

### 1. Home Screen
- Text field: enter username
- "Enter" button → stores username locally, navigates to Session screen
- Shows current active session indicator if one is live

### 2. Session Screen
- Displays username and currently active session (book title + elapsed timer)
- Timer runs entirely on the device — no network call needed to tick
- "Start Reading" button → input book title → generates `clientId` UUID, starts local timer, persists session to local storage, fires first sync (`POST /sessions/sync`)
- "Stop Reading" button (visible when session active) → stops local timer, sets `endedAt`, fires final sync with `endedAt` populated, clears active-session local state
- Periodic background sync every 30 s while a session is active (keeps leaderboard current)
- Link to Leaderboard screen

### 3. Leaderboard Screen
- Tab bar: Daily / Weekly / Monthly / All-time
- Ranked list: `#rank · username · Xh Ym` (formatted from totalSec)
- Auto-refresh via REST polling (on tab focus and every 30 s while visible)
- Highlight current user's row

---

## Docker Compose

```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: bookreads
      POSTGRES_USER: bookreads
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: bookreads
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data

  backend:
    build: ./backend
    depends_on:
      - db
    environment:
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_URL: jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/bookreads
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_USERNAME: bookreads
      SPRING_DATASOURCE_PASSWORD: bookreads
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"

volumes:
  pgdata:
```

---

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1 — Backend Foundation ✓
- [x] Gradle root project + `backend` and `shared-dto` modules
- [x] Docker Compose with PostgreSQL
- [x] SQL init script: `users` + `reading_sessions` tables (with `client_id` unique column), mounted into the PostgreSQL container
- [x] `UserController` + `UserService` + `UserRepository`
- [x] `SessionController` + `SessionService` (`POST /sessions/sync` upsert on `client_id`, `GET /sessions/{clientId}`)
- [x] `LeaderboardController` + `LeaderboardService` (4 time windows, `SUM(duration_sec)`)
- [x] Integration tests (Testcontainers + PostgreSQL)

### Phase 2 — KMP Client Scaffold
- [ ] `client` module with all 4 targets (android, iosArm64/iosX64, jvm, Web)
- [ ] Ktor HTTP client wired to backend
- [ ] Platform storage service interface (`LocalStorageService`) with Koin-injected implementations:
  - `androidMain` / `iosMain` / `jvmMain`: `PrefServiceDataStore` backed by `androidx.datastore.core.okio` (`OkioStorage` + JSON serializer + platform `PrefPathProvider`)
  - `webMain`: `PrefServiceLocalStorage` backed by `window.localStorage` (JS interop)
- [ ] `LocalSessionStore` — persists active session state (clientId, bookTitle, startedAt epoch, elapsed offset) across app restarts
- [ ] `SessionSyncService` — fires `POST /sessions/sync`; retries on failure; schedules periodic 30 s sync while active
- [ ] `UserRepository`, `SessionRepository` (client-side), `LeaderboardRepository` (client-side)
- [ ] Koin modules

### Phase 3 — Compose Multiplatform UI
- [ ] `HomeScreen` with username entry
- [ ] `SessionScreen`: device-local timer via `LaunchedEffect` coroutine ticking every second; start generates clientId + fires first sync; stop fires final sync; timer survives recomposition via `StateFlow`
- [ ] `LeaderboardScreen` with 4-tab view; polls `GET /leaderboard` on tab focus and every 30 s while visible
- [ ] Navigation between screens

### Phase 4 — Platform Entry Points
- [ ] Android `MainActivity`
- [ ] iOS `MainViewController` + Xcode project skeleton
- [ ] JVM Desktop `main()` with `singleWindowApplication`
- [ ] Web `main()` with `CanvasBasedWindow`

### Phase 5 — Polish & Packaging
- [ ] Dockerfile for backend (`./gradlew bootJar` → slim JRE image)
- [ ] Error handling: duplicate username, server unreachable (sync queued locally)
- [ ] Sync retry queue: if `POST /sessions/sync` fails, store pending sync in local storage and retry on next connectivity event
- [ ] README with setup and run instructions

---

## Key Design Decisions

**Client owns session lifecycle** — the device starts the timer, owns the `clientId` UUID, and decides when a session ends. No network call is required to begin or resume reading. This means the app works offline; accumulated time is synced when connectivity returns.

**One active session constraint** — enforced on the client. The client stores at most one active session in local storage. The backend does not check for conflicting active sessions; it blindly upserts on `clientId`.

**Sync strategy** — the client fires `POST /sessions/sync` on start, every 30 s while active (progress update), and immediately on end. This keeps leaderboard data reasonably current for active sessions without requiring a persistent connection for the timer itself.

**`duration_sec` is client-authoritative** — the server stores whatever the client sends. The generated-column approach is dropped; `duration_sec` is a plain `BIGINT` column updated on each upsert. This avoids timezone or rounding mismatches between client and server clocks.

**Leaderboard computation** — computed on read (`SUM(duration_sec)` with `WHERE started_at >= windowStart`), not materialized. Active sessions contribute their last-synced `duration_sec`, so the leaderboard is accurate to within the sync interval.

**Leaderboard polling** — the client polls `GET /leaderboard` when the leaderboard tab becomes visible and every 30 s while it remains on screen. No persistent connection is required; results are accurate to within the polling interval (same as the session sync interval).

**Username as identity** — username is stored in a Kotlin `StateFlow` in the client ViewModel and persisted via `LocalStorageService`. On Android, iOS, and JVM, the implementation uses `androidx.datastore.core.okio` (`DataStoreFactory` + `OkioStorage` + JSON serializer); each platform supplies a `PrefPathProvider` (via Koin) pointing to the appropriate files directory. On Web, the implementation writes directly to `window.localStorage` via JS interop. No `expect/actual` is needed — Koin platform modules wire the concrete class.

**Active session persistence** — the current active session (clientId, bookTitle, startedAt, elapsed offset) is persisted to local storage so a device restart or app kill resumes the in-progress session correctly without data loss.

**Shared DTOs** — `shared-dto` uses only `kotlinx.serialization` annotations. On the backend, Spring's `ObjectMapper` is configured to delegate JSON to kotlinx-serialization. On the client, Ktor's content negotiation uses the same serialization.

1→package com.bookreads.sync
     2→
     3→import com.bookreads.api.BookApi
     4→import com.bookreads.dto.SessionSyncRequest
     5→import com.bookreads.session.LocalSessionStore
     6→import kotlinx.coroutines.CoroutineScope
     7→import kotlinx.coroutines.Job
     8→import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
     9→import kotlinx.coroutines.isActive
    10→import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
    11→import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.first
    12→
    13→class SessionSyncService(
    14→    private val api: BookApi,
    15→    private val sessionStore: LocalSessionStore,
    16→) {
    17→    private var periodicJob: Job? = null
    18→
    19→    suspend fun syncOnce(username: String, endedAt: String? = null) {
    20→        try {
    21→            val session = sessionStore.getActiveSession().first() ?: return
    22→            api.syncSession(
    23→                SessionSyncRequest(
    24→                    clientId = session.clientId,
    25→                    username = username,
    26→                    bookTitle = session.bookTitle,
    27→                    startedAt = session.startedAt,
    28→                    endedAt = endedAt,
    29→                    durationSec = session.elapsedSec,
    30→                )
    31→            )
    32→        } catch (_: Exception) {
    33→        }
    34→    }
    35→
    36→    fun startPeriodicSync(username: String, scope: CoroutineScope) {
    37→        periodicJob?.cancel()
    38→        periodicJob = scope.launch {
    39→            while (isActive) {
    40→                delay(30_000L)
    41→                syncOnce(username)
    42→            }
    43→        }
    44→    }
    45→
    46→    fun stopSync() {
    47→        periodicJob?.cancel()
    48→        periodicJob = null
    49→    }
    50→}
    51→

The `build` task (which includes tests) requires Node.js for wasmJs browser tests. The error is:
```
Could not find org.nodejs:node:25.0.0.
  Searched in the following locations:
    - https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2/org/nodejs/node/25.0.0/node-25.0.0.pom
```

The Kotlin/WasmJS plugin tries to download Node.js from its CDN, but because `PREFER_SETTINGS` mode is active and the Node.js download URL (`https://nodejs.org/dist`) is being blocked, it can't find the Node binary.


The root cause is that `PREFER_SETTINGS` mode blocks the Node.js distribution repository that the Kotlin WasmJS plugin needs for test execution, forcing it to look for the binary in Maven Central where it doesn't exist. Switching `repositoriesMode` to `PREFER_PROJECT` would allow the Node.js CDN to be accessible.

Other approaches would be excluding the `kotlinWasmNodeJsSetup` task from the build, installing Node.js locally, or keeping `PREFER_SETTINGS` but explicitly adding the Node.js distribution URL to the settings repositories. The real issue is that `assemble` works fine since it skips tests, but `build` includes test execution where `wasmJsBrowserTest` requires downloading Node.js through the plugin.

The core problem is that `PREFER_SETTINGS` mode blocks access to the Node.js distribution CDN. I need to figure out how to properly configure the repositories so that `PREFER_SETTINGS` doesn't prevent the Kotlin plugin from downloading Node.js while still keeping the Google Maven repository accessible for `androidx.datastore`. The original issue was that project-level repositories were overriding the settings-level `google()` repository, which `PREFER_SETTINGS` fixed, but now it's blocking the Node.js download that the Kotlin plugin needs. I'm realizing the real problem might have been the `content` filtering on the `google()` repository in the original settings—that could have been preventing the androidx.datastore dependency from being found. Let me trace back through what actually happened: the first error about the missing dependency occurred without `PREFER_SETTINGS`, then adding `PREFER_SETTINGS` triggered a different error about the ktlint script, which suggests the repository configuration itself might have been the core issue all along. through:

Before `PREFER_SETTINGS`:
- `dependencyResolutionManagement.repositories` has `google()` with content filter for `androidx.*`
- AGP adds project-level repos to `:client`
- Default `PREFER_PROJECT` mode means `:client` uses its own repos, not the settings repos
- AGP's project repos might be empty or only have some repos
- Result: `androidx.datastore` not found

After `PREFER_SETTINGS`:
- `dependencyResolutionManagement.repositories` take precedence, including `google()` for `androidx.*`
- `ktlint.gradle` warns about adding `MavenRepo` but it's ignored (warning only)
